newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids fall further.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids fall further.

text.p: Bids for dark northern spring wheat fell further on Monday in reaction to weak demand and USDA's spring wheat plantings forecast which put acreage above expectations, cash dealers said.
"All the farmers want to talk about is the acreage," a Minnesota dealer said. "I think they're all just in shell shock. There's a lot of grain still out there and obviously a lot in the field."
USDA on Monday put spring wheat plantings at 19.1 million acres, above expectations for 18.1 million.
But some dealers noted quality concerns. A North Dakota dealer reported large drowned-out areas and a Montana merchant said farmers were concerned about low protein levels.
USDA on Monday said spring wheat conditions declined in the week ended Sunday with 50 percent rated good to excellent versus 52 percent the previous week.

"I think a lot of farmers don't want to sell the new crop because they don't know what kind of proteins they'll have," a Montana dealer said. "And if they have any old crop at 12, 13 or 14 percent, they're going to hold on to it."
